I have implemented [jump_analyzer.py](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-gs9gpwho/jump_analyzer.py) (mounted at `/app/jump_analyzer.py` inside the container) and verified it against [example_video.mp4](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-gs9gpwho/example_video.mp4).

### How It Works
1. **Camera Stabilization & Background Subtraction**: [`analyze_video`](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-gs9gpwho/jump_analyzer.py#L10-L98) aligns each frame to the empty initial background frame (`frame 0`) via phase correlation on the foreground track strip (`y >= 0.70 * H`) and compensates for global illumination shifts before computing per-pixel color differences.
2. **Athlete Segmentation**: Morphological opening and dilation followed by connected-component analysis (`cv2.connectedComponentsWithStats`) isolates the athlete across frames and extracts the horizontal centroid (`x_mean`) and vertical bounds (`y_min`, `y_max`).
3. **Takeoff & Landing Detection**: The script identifies the peak airborne frame (`t_peak`) over the hurdle where the lowest point of the athlete (`y_max`) reaches its minimum, determines the stance ground levels immediately preceding and following the jump, and locates `jump_takeoff_frame_number` (last frame of ground contact prior to flight) and `jump_land_frame_number` (first frame of ground contact upon landing), writing the result to [output.toml](file:///tmp/xhs-c6-host-gs9gpwho/output.toml) (`/app/output.toml`).
